name: Medina of Fez
description: Tucked among the hills of northern Morocco, the Medina of Fez is a walled old city of winding, car-free lanes, one of the largest pedestrian zones in the world. Founded around the 9th century, it holds the al-Qarawiyyin university, dating from 857, and the Chouara Tannery's dye pits. Its madrasas, mosques and fountains largely date from the 13th–14th centuries, when Fez was the Marinid capital.
